feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 2 (±0.06 m span, y = 0.03, 16 mm, 0.10 m track) had line_loss_events 0 on all tracks, but max_error stayed at 0.0609 to 0.0614, the same floor as iteration 1, and oval progress stayed at 0.115. Slalom progress fell from 0.105 (iteration 1) to 0.035, so the wider span helped sensing but hurt slalom. Iteration 1 had steering_oscillation 0.159 on slalom. What I had to do: I kept the span, footprint and y row so the wheel_track change is the only geometry difference. I raised ki from 0.05 to 0.5 to cancel a steady drift that kp alone cannot remove, and left kp at 2.5 because slalom oscillation was already near 0.16. Next race, if max_error on oval and s-bend drops below about 0.055 with progress past 0.115, keep wheel_track 0.12 and try the next step at 0.14. If max_error still sits at about 0.061, the drift is not a track-width effect, so change wheel_radius rather than widening further. If slalom progress stays near 0.035, the ±0.06 span is costing slalom, so test ±0.05 at y = 0.03.
requested_changes: If max_error drops below about 0.055 on oval and s-bend with wheel_track 0.12, try wheel_track 0.14 with the ±0.06 span kept, because iteration 2 showed max_error pinned at 0.061 at 0.10 m and a wider track lowers yaw per unit of mismatch.

If max_error stays at about 0.061 with wheel_track 0.12, change wheel_radius to 0.035 (keeping wheel_track 0.12), because the floor did not move between iterations 1 and 2 when only the span changed and the track alone may not be the lever.

If slalom progress stays below about 0.06 with the ±0.06 span, reduce the outer sensors to x = ±0.05 at y = 0.03, because iteration 1 (±0.04) reached slalom progress 0.110 while iteration 2 (±0.06) reached 0.035 with line losses already at 0.
